flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between price and cost?
flashcard_questions.a: Price is what the customer pays; cost is what the business spends.
Setting a high price at launch and gradually lowering it over time.
Working out the total cost of making a product and adding a profit margin.
Setting a low initial price to attract customers quickly and build market share.
Setting prices at a similar level to rival businesses.
Selling a product below cost to attract customers into the store.
Making a price appear lower, such as charging £9.99 instead of £10.00.
A product gets smaller while its price stays the same.

flashcard_questions.q: Which company used price skimming when it launched the Xbox One?
Which streaming service used penetration pricing to win subscribers at launch?
Which retailer sells rotisserie chickens at a loss to drive footfall?
Which industry most commonly uses cost-plus pricing?
What is the main advantage of price skimming for a new product?
flashcard_questions.a: Early adopters pay top price, which is very profitable.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main disadvantage of penetration pricing at launch?
flashcard_questions.a: Profit margins are very low during the launch period.

flashcard_questions.q: What risk does a business take when it uses a loss leader?
flashcard_questions.a: Customers may buy only that product and never return.

notes: 15 cards: 8 term→definition covering all five strategies plus price/cost, psychological pricing and shrinkflation, 4 concept→named example (Microsoft Xbox One, Disney+, Costco, food industry), 3 single-fact advantage/disadvantage cards. The four influences on pricing were left as separate teaching content rather than one list card — an enumeration answer cannot be self-graded.
